title: Coefficient-preserving stratified reduction and finite Postnikov comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $A=\mathcal O_E$, and a scheme $T$, using fixed small pro-étale skeletons [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every scheme $W$ put $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/\ell^n}_W$ and $R_{W,n}=\underline{A/\ell^n}_W$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and derived scalar extension computed by K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D(R_T)$ have cohomology supported in a finite interval $[r,s]$. Suppose given a finite partition of $T$ by constructible locally closed subschemes with actual immersions $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to T$ [def-constructible-stratification], and suppose every $i_\alpha^*H^q(M)$ has a finite constant local model over $R_{S_\alpha}$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use the canonical coefficient identifications $i_\alpha^{-1}R_T\simeq R_{S_\alpha}$ and $i_\alpha^{-1}R_{T,n}\simeq R_{S_\alpha,n}$, so that $i_\alpha^*$ is exact inverse image with its transported scalar action.

For every $n\geq1$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(R_{S_\alpha,n})$
$$i_\alpha^*(M\otimes_{R_T}^LR_{T,n})\simeq (i_\alpha^*M)\otimes_{R_{S_\alpha}}^LR_{S_\alpha,n},$$
compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles. The reductions followed by restriction of the canonical truncation triangles
$$\tau_{\leq q-1}M\longrightarrow\tau_{\leq q}M\longrightarrow H^q(M)[-q]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\leq q-1}M)[1]$$
[def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] are a finite sequence of distinguished triangles, starting at zero for $q=r$ and ending at the restricted reduction of $M$ for $q=s$. Every term in this sequence has locally constant finite-type cohomology on $S_\alpha$; the final term has cohomology only in $[r-1,s]$. In particular every cohomology sheaf of $M\otimes_{R_T}^LR_{T,n}$ is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], using this same finite global partition for all $n$ and all degrees, with finite geometric stalks on each stratum. No identification of truncation with derived reduction is asserted; only the images of the truncation triangles are used. No qcqs or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ is required beyond the explicitly given finite global partition. The zero complex and the empty scheme are included.

proof.text: Coefficient preparation (formalized in this delivery). Construct the constant-scalar cone with NatTrans.ofOpSequence: adjacent quotient maps compose to the lower quotient map, and faithfulness of commutative-ring forgetting identifies these components with the specified preimages. Apply the constant-ring inverse-image naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] at each adjacent quotient and NatTrans.ofOpSequence to obtain spStratifiedFiniteMap_naturality for every tower arrow. For each ell-power quotient, use cofinality [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] to choose a uniformizer-power ideal contained in its defining ideal; the finite coefficient quotient [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] surjects onto it, proving finiteness. Express the given commutative coefficient tower as the constant sheaf of its finite ring tower, using identity component isomorphisms. The inverse-image functor preserves its limit by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-tower-limit]. Its mapped limit cone and the target limit cone are identified by the canonical finite constant-ring isomorphisms. Mathlib conePointsIsoOfNatIso gives an isomorphism of their cone points. Its projection equations agree with those of spStratifiedRingMap, so limit.hom_ext identifies the canonical limit lift with its hom, proving spStratifiedRingMap_isIso. The remaining six steps below retain the plan for the three still-open comparison/Postnikov declarations.

proof.text: Fix a stratum $i:S\to T$ and $n\geq1$, and use the coefficient identifications specified in the statement. By [def-sfb-proetale-ring-derived-inverse-image], applied to $i$ with $R=R_T$ and with $R=R_{T,n}$, module inverse image is additive and exact over the actual inverse-image rings $i^{-1}R_T$, $i^{-1}R_{T,n}$, and it acts termwise on complexes. Transporting scalars along the given ring isomorphisms $i^{-1}R_T\simeq R_S$, $i^{-1}R_{T,n}\simeq R_{S,n}$ is an equivalence of module categories, so $i^*$ is exact for both $R_T$ and $R_{T,n}$. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c), $H^k(i^*K)\simeq i^*H^k(K)$ naturally, so termwise inverse image preserves quasi-isomorphisms. It therefore acts on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. It commutes with shifts and cone triangles: apply its additivity to the matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ defining the cone in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This gives exactly the cone matrix of $i^*f$, including its inclusion and negative projection. Hence derived inverse image is exact, with these specified shift maps.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), transported coefficients; cone and homology calculation

proof.text: Choose $P\to M$ K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Exact inverse image makes $i^*P\to i^*M$ a quasi-isomorphism; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], with the coefficient isomorphism as ring map, makes $i^*P$ K-flat with flat terms. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the two objects to compare are represented by $i^*(P\otimes_{R_T}R_{T,n})$ and $(i^*P)\otimes_{R_S}R_{S,n}$. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] identifies them degreewise by $i^{-1}(x\otimes a)\mapsto i^{-1}x\otimes i^{-1}a$. This is $R_{S,n}$-linear: multiplying the second tensor factor by $c$ gives the same formula with $ac$ on both sides. The formula commutes with differentials and maps of resolutions. The resolving-class equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and the transformation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descend it to a natural isomorphism on $D(R_T)$. The formula in each shifted degree is unchanged and commutes with the negative shifted differential; on a cone it is the direct sum of the two component formulas and commutes with the off-diagonal map. Thus it respects shifts and cone triangles, including connecting maps. Both reduction functors are exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and restriction is exact by step 1, so this proves the stated compatibility with distinguished triangles.

Put $F_{i,n}(K)=i^*(K\otimes^L_{R_T}R_{T,n})$. Apply this exact functor to [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], for $q=r,\ldots,s$. Write $X_q=F_{i,n}(\tau_{\leq q}M)$ and $B_q=F_{i,n}(H^q(M)[-q])$. This yields distinguished triangles $X_{q-1}\to X_q\to B_q\to X_{q-1}[1]$. The explicit truncations in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] have the same cohomology as $M$ in degrees at most $q$, and zero above $q$. Thus $\tau_{\leq r-1}M$ is acyclic and the canonical $\tau_{\leq s}M\to M$ is a quasi-isomorphism, by the given support interval. In the localization defining the derived category these identify $X_{r-1}=0$ and $X_s\simeq F_{i,n}(M)$. This is a finite sequence of images of truncation triangles; no truncation of a reduction is substituted for any $X_q$.

proof.text: Let $L_q=i^*H^q(M)$, which has the finite constant local model supplied in the hypotheses. Step 2 and shift compatibility identify $B_q\simeq(L_q[0]\otimes^L_{R_S}R_{S,n})[-q]$. Apply [lem-sp-integral-local-model-finite-matrix-reduction] on the arbitrary scheme $S$. It gives locally constant finite-type cohomology of the unshifted reduction only in degrees $-1,0$, on local covers independent of $n$, and gives finiteness of $A_n=A/\ell^n$. Consequently $B_q$ has locally constant finite-type cohomology only in degrees $q-1,q$. This uses finite constant models rather than an assumption that $L_q$ is torsion-free; the degree $q-1$ is retained.

proof.text:
For fixed $i,n$, let $\mathcal L_n$ be the locally constant finite-type $\underline{A_n}$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The finite ring $A_n$ is Noetherian: it has only finitely many ideals, so every ascending ideal chain stabilizes. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] applies on this small site. Induct on $q=r,\ldots,s$, with $X_{r-1}=0$, claiming all $H^k(X_q)$ lie in $\mathcal L_n$ and vanish outside $[r-1,q]$. For the triangle of step 3, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the short exact sequence
$$0\to\operatorname{coker}(H^{k-1}(B_q)\to H^k(X_{q-1}))\to H^k(X_q)\to\ker(H^k(B_q)\to H^{k+1}(X_{q-1}))\to0.$$
Its outer terms lie in $\mathcal L_n$ by kernel/cokernel closure and the inductive hypothesis together with step 4; extension closure gives the middle term. Outside $[r-1,q]$, both $H^k(X_{q-1})$ and $H^k(B_q)$ vanish, so exactness gives $H^k(X_q)=0$. The base is zero cohomology, which is constant of finite type. This proves the claim and gives $[r-1,s]$ for $X_s$. All the $B_q$, the $X_q$, and their shifted fourth terms have locally constant finite-type cohomology, since shifting merely reindexes the degrees.

By step 1, $i_\alpha^*H^k(M\otimes^L_{R_T}R_{T,n})\simeq H^k(F_{i_\alpha,n}(M))$. Step 5 makes this locally constant of finite type for every $\alpha,n,k$. Its geometric stalks are finite: on a constant chart a finitely generated $A_n$-module is a quotient of $A_n^t$ for finite $t$, hence is a finite set. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-model-stalks] to these finite constant models to obtain finite geometric stalks. Therefore the very partition in the hypotheses satisfies [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] for all the reduced cohomology sheaves. The indices $n,k$ never required a new partition. Nothing in these arguments uses qcqs or Noetherianity of $T$ or $S_\alpha$: Noetherianity was used only for the finite scalar ring $A_n$. For $M=0$ all terms are zero; for empty $T$ (represented by its single empty stratum) all restrictions and stalk assertions are vacuous, so these cases are included.
